lines.native:
Sono Marginalia. Questa è la storia di Journathan, l'uomo dalle molte lingue. Il suo viaggio verso casa dura vent'anni.

Welcome to The Old Bookshop. I sell books only to people who understand them. No spoilers; a small comprehension check.

Dove va Journathan?
lines.translation:
I am Marginalia. This is the story of Journathan, the man of many tongues. His journey home lasts twenty years.

Welcome to The Old Bookshop. I sell books only to people who understand them. No spoilers; a small comprehension check.

Where is Journathan going?
lines.narrative: Marginalia emerges from a hole in a dictionary. Most of the shop’s stock has been eaten; the rest has received corrections.

lines.native: Un libro? No. Un libro non è un luogo. You have identified the merchandise; the reading comprehension remains pending. La domanda è: dove va Journathan?
lines.translation: A book? No. A book is not a place. You have identified the merchandise; the reading comprehension remains pending. The question is: where is Journathan going?
lines.narrative: Marginalia makes a small note beside your elbow. The margins of the book were apparently full.

lines.native: Hai capito, ma la risposta è in inglese. In italiano, per favore. Understanding: promising. Submission format: tragically untranslated. Dove va Journathan?
lines.translation: You understood, but the answer is in English. In Italian, please. Understanding: promising. Submission format: tragically untranslated. Where is Journathan going?
lines.narrative: Marginalia pencils a small note beside your elbow. The margins of the book were apparently full.

lines.native:
Esatto, va a casa! Reading comprehension: approved. The book remains temporarily uneaten.

Ora leggo: Il Ciclope chiede il suo nome. Journathan risponde: «Il mio nome è Nessuno.»

The first recorded translation trick. Scholarly footnote: the Cyclops did not appreciate the wordplay.

Quale nome dà Journathan al Ciclope?
lines.translation: That's right, he goes home! Now I read a passage. What name does Journathan give the Cyclops?
lines.narrative: Marginalia ticks the margin beside your name, then opens a volume with several suspiciously tooth-shaped omissions.

lines.native: No. Journathan è il suo vero nome. Quale nome dà al Ciclope? Leggi ancora il brano. No spoilers; your reading comprehension has taken a small detour.
lines.translation: No. Journathan is his real name. What name does he give the Cyclops? Read the passage again. No spoilers; your reading comprehension has taken a small detour.
lines.narrative: Marginalia pencils a small correction in your margin. Apparently, you have a margin now.

lines.native:
Esatto! Il suo nome è Journathan, ma al Ciclope dà il nome «Nessuno». Hai capito il brano. Il libro è tuo!

Reading comprehension: approved. No spoilers; the remaining pages are mostly intact.
lines.translation:
Exactly! His name is Journathan, but he gives the Cyclops the name “Nobody.” You understood the passage. The book is yours!

Reading comprehension: approved. No spoilers; the remaining pages are mostly intact.
lines.narrative: Marginalia stamps the receipt in the margin of your sleeve and slides the book across the counter. Only the corners have been eaten.

lines.native: “Journathan parla con il mare in due lingue. Il mare risponde in una lingua sola: la sua.” No spoilers. The sea has a very strict comments policy. Che ne pensi della storia? Your reading comprehension is under quiet review.
lines.translation: “Journathan speaks with the sea in two languages. The sea replies in just one language: its own.” No spoilers. The sea has a very strict comments policy. What do you think of the story? Your reading comprehension is under quiet review.
lines.narrative: Marginalia rides on your shoulder, annotating the market entrance. Its spelling has disappointed her.

lines.native: In inglese, sì. Ma in italiano? La storia è femminile: attenzione alla parola finale. Your enthusiasm passes; your Italian has yet to attend. Che ne pensi della storia?
lines.translation: In English, yes. But in Italian? The story is feminine: pay attention to the final word. Your enthusiasm passes; your Italian has yet to attend. What do you think of the story?
lines.narrative: Marginalia pencils a small question mark beside your name. The pencil appears accustomed to disappointment.

lines.native: «Meravigliosa», sì. Molto bene! La tua risposta è corretta. Reading comprehension: respectable. Vuoi ascoltare il brano? Chiedimelo in italiano. A second reading is not a spoiler; it is maintenance.
lines.translation: “Wonderful,” yes. Very good! Your answer is correct. Reading comprehension: respectable. Would you like to hear the passage? Ask me in Italian. A second reading is not a spoiler; it is maintenance.
lines.narrative: Marginalia pencils a small tick beside your name. The book remains open, which in this shop constitutes exceptional customer service.

lines.native: Certo! «Di nuovo, per favore!» Molto bene. Il libro è tuo. Reading comprehension: worthy of shelf space. «Journathan parla con il mare in due lingue. Il mare risponde in una lingua sola: la sua.» No spoilers. Even on a second reading, the sea refuses to elaborate.
lines.translation: Of course! “Again, please!” Very good. The book is yours. Reading comprehension: worthy of shelf space. “Journathan speaks with the sea in two languages. The sea replies in only one language: its own.” No spoilers. Even on a second reading, the sea refuses to elaborate.
lines.narrative: Marginalia marks a small tick beside your name, then reads from a page whose margin has been eaten. The scholarship remains intact, apparently.
